definition: An informal mutual aid web operating across the Shelf and lower Old Harbor, distributing medical supplies, food, and black-market BCI patches through a decentralized chain of trusted carriers. Named for the green-painted markers left on walls to indicate safe hand-off points.
origin: Street cant; originated in the Gulch around 2188 as a response to Carrion Logistics monopolizing supply routes into Tier 1 zones
usage: Tier 1 communities, activist medics, sympathetic Tier 2 workers; deliberately unknown to corporate and security forces
example: Her kid needed Helix-grade antivirals and she couldn't touch a licensed pharmacy — Verdigris Network had a drop two blocks over, no questions, sliding scale.
